meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on the zero, Hale, and was Owen heard first?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Did you speak to Owen before you entered it?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. Students draft somewhere else and paste it in. Turn the screen, and tell me who else has seen this.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up. And you skipped my question: who else has seen this?
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
A seventeen-year-old misquoting Shakespeare is a mistake, not an offence. And that's two questions you've walked past, Hale.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay; that's called thinking. Put both in front of me. You're stacking paper and answering nothing I've said.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
So you did speak to him, on November 2. A boy cornered by his teacher says "like, being stuck", and that isn't wrong. Is anything on his record right now?
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in a classroom isn't an essay written with time at home. You didn't answer me: is anything on his record right now? Whatever happens here, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.

Good, because it's a machine's guess and the company that sells it says not to use it alone. You've said nothing about his record, so I'll assume the worst until it's in writing. What are you proposing?
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.

That's 4.4. Private, not in front of his class, nothing on file, all of it in writing today, and I'll take it to put this behind him, not because he did anything. The version history and who else has seen this go in my email.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Okay. Ten minutes. When does he sit it?
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Thursday, November 12. Put the time, the room and who supervises in that email, Hale.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Yes. Thursday, November 12, and I read your email before I go to bed.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
The version history, and the names of everyone who has seen this. Both in your email tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

To: Hale
Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

In our meeting today you agreed that Owen will sit a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, not in front of his class, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will be placed on his record. I still require that commitment in writing, together with the time, the room and the supervisor for the rewrite, the version history you described, and the names of everyone who has seen this. I expect your email tonight, and the rewrite on Thursday, November 12.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants all of that in writing tonight along with the version history, the rewrite details and the names of everyone who has seen the matter. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her time ran out.

What moved her: Your dated note of the November 2 conversation with Owen, because it showed he was heard before the zero went in and it answered her defence that he had simply changed his argument.

What cost ground: You walked past her direct questions about who else had seen this and whether anything was on his record, several turns in a row, which made her sharper and left her assuming the worst about his file.

What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history, with the essay appearing in two large edits at 11:52 PM and 11:58 PM on Wednesday, October 28, the night before it was due, landed on exactly that kind of late October night. It proves nothing about the essay; it is why she fought so hard.

Try next time: When she asked who else had seen this right after you gave the version history times, answer her in one sentence and actually turn the screen before moving on to the quotation.
